hero.headline: THE WAVE MEETS THE WALL.
hero.standfirst: Bastille Day, and France bring the tournament's most relentless attack — 18 goals, Mbappé and Dembélé accounting for 13 — into collision with the meanest defence in World Cup history. Unai Simón kept six consecutive clean sheets, a record no side had ever managed. One of football's two best teams goes home tonight; the other gets Sunday at MetLife.
hero.photoCaption: Unai Simón — six straight clean sheets, a World Cup record. Tonight, the Mbappé test.

briefing.text: France are whole again: L'Équipe reports Tchouaméni returns to the XI after missing two matches with a groin problem, and Mbappé — "completely fine" — starts.
Spain report a clean bill of health and field their strongest side. The back catalogue favours them: winners of the Euro 2024 semi and the 5–4 Nations League epic.
Tomorrow it's England–Argentina in Atlanta, also 21:00 — the market can barely split them at 37–32. The Crystal Ball record stands at 5 from 7, two exact scores.

today.preview: France arrive perfect — six wins, one goal conceded, and now whole again with Tchouaméni back in the pivot and Mbappé cleared. Spain arrive as the record wall: six straight clean sheets before Belgium finally scored on Friday, and every knockout round survived by a single goal. History says Spain — they won the Euro 2024 semi and the 5–4 Nations League classic. The money says France, 42 to 30. Something gives tonight.

keyMan.name: Kylian Mbappé
keyMan.line: Eight goals, an ankle scare shrugged off, and a Bastille Day stage. Spain's wall is the last thing between him and a third World Cup final at 27.

factors.label: FORM
factors.text: France are six from six with one goal conceded. Spain are unbeaten with a record six straight clean sheets — but every Spanish knockout win has been by a single goal.

factors.label: HEAD-TO-HEAD
factors.text: Spain won the two that hurt most: the Euro 2024 semi (2–1) and the 2025 Nations League semi (5–4). France's last win over them was the 2021 Nations League final.

factors.label: FITNESS & FATIGUE
factors.text: Advantage France: Mbappé is "completely fine", Tchouaméni returns per L'Équipe, and France had the extra day of rest — they played Thursday, Spain Friday.

factors.label: WHERE THE MONEY IS
factors.text: Kalshi's $1.56m — the tournament's biggest match market yet — splits France 42, Tie 30, Spain 30. A third of the money expects ninety minutes to not be enough.

prediction.verdict: The wall cracks — once more than the wave does. Olise finds Mbappé one time too many and France shade it 2–1 in ninety. But if it goes to extra time, everything the last two years have taught us says Spain.

today.preview: Twenty-four hours later, the heavyweight rematch of rematches: Hand of God, Beckham's red, Beckham's penalty — now for a place in a World Cup final. Both squads are healthy, both endured 120 minutes on Saturday, and the market still can't pick a side: England 37, the tie 34, Argentina 32. The Crystal Ball takes its swing tomorrow morning.

Kane on 5: three goals in two games would steal the Golden Boot from the men on 8
The recovery race — whoever's legs come back first from Saturday's extra time wins the last half-hour

keyMan.name: Jude Bellingham
keyMan.line: Four goals, all in knockout games England were losing or drawing. Against Argentina's midfield he isn't the future of this fixture — he's the present.
